newsitem.title: USA: NTSB finds break, crack in rail side bar.
newsitem.headline: NTSB finds break, crack in rail side bar.

text.p: Investigators found a break and a crack in two side rails at the point where an Amtrak passenger train travelling from Washington to Boston Saturday went off the tracks, the National Transportation Safety Board said Monday.

Six cars of the 14-car train plunged down an embankment into a marsh near the Hackensack River drawbridge about three miles west of New York City, causing no serious injuries but disrupting rail traffic in the busy northeast corridor for more than 24 hours.
"NTSB investigators discovered one broken and one cracked rail side bar on the bridge miter rail at the point of derailment," the board said in a written statement.
The side bars have been sent to NTSB laboratories in Washington for analysis along with the train's event recorders, devices similar to the so-called black boxes installed on aircraft.
The NTSB said investigators had tested the mechanism of the open deck swivel bridge, inspected the accident site and interviewed railroad personnel.
They will study the information on the event recorders and examine maintenance and inspection records before drawing any conclusions about the possible cause of the accident.
"We will also be reviewing the current standards and guidelines for conducting maintenance and inspections on the rail line," the NTSB statement said.

The train was carrying 115 passengers when the accident occurred early Saturday morning. The two locomotives and four passenger cars derailed, went down an embankment and came to rest on their sides. The other cars derailed but remained upright.
The NTSB said 36 people were taken to area hospitals and two were admitted. About 60 people were treated and released at the accident scene by local emergency medical units.
Amtrak reopened full train service along the northeast corridor late Sunday.
